chunks: Ibn Abi Umayr from Ibn Bukayr from Zurara from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) in

Regarding a woman who lost her husband or news of his death was brought to her, so she married, then her husband returned after that and divorced her, he said: She observes a single waiting period from both of them together, which is three months, and the latter [husband] cannot marry her ever.
ai.seo_question: What is the waiting period and marital status for a woman whose first husband returns after she married a second man due to his presumed death?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Istibsar clarifies the specific case of 'ghayb' (presumed death) where a woman marries a second husband after her first husband is missing, only for the first to return and issue a divorce (not a full dissolution). It establishes that she observes a single, unified waiting period of three months and years, covering both marital bonds, and crucially, the second husband is permanently barred from remarrying her, distinguishing this from the standard 'khula' or 'talaq' scenarios. This ruling highlights the Shia juristic emphasis on the continuity of the woman's status and the finality of the second marriage in this unique context.
